title: Operator scope lock and KMS jurisdiction handoff
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds operator-scoped RBAC lock, a KMS jurisdiction handoff middleware, and audit enrichment to record region assertions and KMS origin for compliance and post-incident analysis.
body:
Context and motivation: We saw an operational gap where operator credentials could be applied across tenant geozones when debugging live workloads. This made it hard to guarantee jurisdictional guarantees for KMS-backed keys and produced noisy audit trails during compliance reviews. This PR introduces two complementary controls: 1) an operator scope lock that binds operator elevation to a geographic jurisdiction claim (region), and 2) a KMS jurisdiction handoff middleware that attaches authoritative KMS origin metadata to encryption/decryption requests used by the runtime. Together these changes reduce cross-region operator blast radius and make KMS usage auditable for residency controls.

What this changes (summary):
- services/authz/operator_lock: add operator scope lock and enforcement logic. The lock is a guarded elevation path that validates operator request scopes against the tenant's pinned region claims.
- services/kms/jurisdiction_handoff: middleware that augments KMS requests with kms_origin, kms_region and proof_token when available. Supports multi-provider handshake for cross-account CMKs.
- middleware/audit/enrichers: add region_assertion and kms_origin fields into structured audit events, persisted in the audit forwarder.
- policy/opa/rbacv2: policy templates updated to include operator_scope bindings and a feature-flag gated check (feature.rbac.operator_scope_lock).
- helm/redwood-private-installer: add config toggles and RBAC seed job for operator-scoped roles (examples and migration job).
- tests: unit + integration tests for enforcement, and a small e2e scenario in eval-harness/fixtures to validate KMS handoff headers and audit entries.

Review thread (highlights, chronological):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) add a histogram for operator-elevation attempts by region in the metrics package; (2) ensure the migration job is idempotent if run twice during installer upgrades."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added op_elevation_attempts histogram and made migration job guarded by a JobConfigMap check. Pushed fix in c3b4ea2 -> f0c9aa1."
- Elena García (reviewer): "Policy looks good. Please add a short note to docs/ops/security.md explaining how to roll back if the gate accidentally blocks needed operator flows."
- Maya Chen: "Added rollback steps and a troubleshooting subsection to docs/ops/security.md. Highlighted the feature flag and ClusterRole binding to toggle behavior."
- Samir Venkataraman (approver): "Verified integration tests locally against mock KMS. Approving pending CI green."
- CI: initial run had a lint warning for a missing comment and a flaky test (integration timing). Fixed and re-ran. Final CI status: pass.

Security and compliance notes:
- Threat model update (SEC-77) attached: reduces cross-region operator risk by binding operator tokens to a claim asserted by the API gateway and validated against tenant metadata.
- Audit trail now records authoritative kms_origin and region_assertion tags for every KMS call made through runtime; these are exported to the audit-forwarder and available in the tenant audit UI.
- KMS jurisdiction handoff supports both AWS and GCP CMKs via a provider adapter; providers must opt-in via the installer values to enable cross-account proof tokens.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable feature.rbac.operator_scope_lock for a single non-production tenant in us-east-1, validate operator elevation metrics and audit entries for two weeks.
- Stage 2: gradually enable for internal SRE and Platform teams across two regions after running migration job.
- Stage 3: enable by default when policy is marked stable (post 4 weeks of canary without issues).

Migration considerations:
- The migration job seeds operator-scoped ClusterRoles for known operator principals. The job is guarded and idempotent; it will not remove existing roles. Operators can roll back by removing the feature flag and running the provided rollback script in docs/ops/security.md.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge. Commit message: "operator: introduce operator scope lock and kms jurisdiction handoff; audit enrichment (SEC-77)". PR closed and merged on 2026-02-12 after approvals from Arjun, Elena, and Samir.

Notes for future work:
- Add a runtime sidecar to provide signed region assertions for on-prem deployments that cannot reach the central gateway.
- Add automated policy-lint rules that fail CI when operator_scope bindings are missing for new operator-related code paths.

If any post-merge issues are observed (audit gaps, installer errors) please tag ENG-1029 and SEC-77 in the incident ticket so we can prioritize a hotfix.
